prompt: Shoppers type free-text queries like "red waterproof jacket" and expect relevant results, tolerating typos.
why: An inverted index with relevance ranking and fuzzy matching (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch).
trap: SQL LIKE '%red%' scans everything and has no idea of relevance.

prompt: Engineers search terabytes of logs by keyword and filter by service and time range.
tells: search terabytes of logs by keyword
filter by service and time range
why: Index log lines into a search engine with fields for filtering.
trap: Object storage keeps logs cheaply, but finding a keyword means scanning them all.

prompt: A real-estate site needs search with filters for price, bedrooms and neighborhood, plus counts next to each filter option.
tells: filters for price, bedrooms and neighborhood
counts next to each filter option
why: Faceted search: the index computes counts per facet value alongside results.
trap: Location is one filter, but the core need is faceted search.

prompt: A help center has 50,000 articles and users search them by phrases like "reset password".
why: Full-text index with stemming so "resetting passwords" still matches.
trap: Autocomplete prefixes aren't the same as finding articles that contain phrases.
